course.title: Continental Cooking
course.tagline: Cook pasta, rice dishes, chicken and continental favourites with real flavour.

days.title: Continental Cooking: What Is It?
days.goal: Know what continental cooking means.

video.title: How to Make Pasta at Home By Food Fusion | Easy Step-by-Step Tutorial

steps: Continental means food from Europe and America: pasta, rice dishes, chicken, and more.
It uses olive oil, butter, herbs, and cheese a lot.
It is different from Nigerian food, but the skills are the same.
Learn the main ingredients: pasta, rice, chicken, tomatoes, and cheese.
Taste a pasta dish and a rice dish. Note the flavours.
days.task: List five continental dishes you know.
days.challenge: Taste a pasta dish and write down what you like about it.

quiz.q: What is continental cooking?
options: Food from Europe and America: pasta, rice, chicken, and more
quiz.explain: Continental cooking covers European and American dishes like pasta and roast chicken.

quiz.q: What ingredients does continental cooking use a lot?
options: Olive oil, butter, herbs, and cheese
quiz.explain: Olive oil, butter, herbs, and cheese are common in continental cooking.

quiz.q: Why learn continental cooking?
options: So you can cook for more customers and events
quiz.explain: Continental dishes open up more customers and events.

days.title: How to Cook Pasta Properly
days.goal: Cook pasta that is firm, not soft.

video.title: Easy Homemade Pasta Recipe | From Scratch in No Time!

steps: Use a large pot with plenty of salted water.
Add pasta only when the water is at a full rolling boil.
Stir in the first minute so it does not stick together.
Taste a piece 1 minute before the packet time. It should be firm, not soft.
Save a cup of pasta water to loosen the sauce.
days.task: Cook spaghetti and toss it in a simple tomato sauce.
days.challenge: Cook the pasta so it finishes in the sauce, not in the water.

quiz.q: When should pasta go into the pot?
options: When the water is at a full rolling boil
quiz.explain: Boiling water sets the pasta so it does not clump.

quiz.q: What does 'al dente' mean?
quiz.explain: Al dente is Italian for 'firm to the bite', the right texture for pasta.

quiz.q: Why save pasta water?
options: Its starch helps the sauce stick to the pasta
quiz.explain: Starchy pasta water helps sauce coat the pasta.

days.title: Spaghetti with Tomato Sauce
days.goal: Make spaghetti with a simple tomato sauce.

video.title: Easy Recipe Pasta Carbonara Italian Cooking

steps: Boil spaghetti in salted water until firm.
Fry garlic in olive oil for 30 seconds. Do not let it burn.
Add chopped tomatoes and cook for 10 minutes.
Add salt, pepper, and fresh basil.
Toss the pasta in the sauce with a splash of pasta water.
days.task: Cook spaghetti with tomato sauce.
days.challenge: Add grated cheese on top and serve.

quiz.q: Why fry garlic only briefly?
options: Garlic burns fast and tastes bitter
quiz.explain: Garlic burns in under a minute and turns bitter.

quiz.q: Why add pasta water to the sauce?
options: It helps the sauce stick to the pasta
quiz.explain: Pasta water helps the sauce coat the pasta evenly.

quiz.q: What herb goes well with tomato sauce?
quiz.explain: Basil is the classic herb with tomato sauce.

days.title: Pasta Carbonara: The Classic
days.goal: Make pasta carbonara the real way.

video.title: How To Make Italian Spaghetti with Tomato Sauce / Kids Favourite

steps: Carbonara uses eggs, cheese, and bacon, not cream.
Fry bacon or pancetta until crisp. Set aside.
Whisk eggs with grated cheese and pepper.
Cook pasta. Drain, keeping a cup of pasta water.
Toss hot pasta with bacon, then add the egg mix off the heat.
days.task: Make pasta carbonara.
days.challenge: Taste it and note how creamy it is without cream.

quiz.q: What is in real carbonara?
options: Eggs, cheese, and bacon, not cream
quiz.explain: Real carbonara uses eggs, cheese, and bacon. No cream.

quiz.q: Why add the egg mix off the heat?
options: So the eggs do not turn into scrambled eggs
quiz.explain: Hot pasta cooks the eggs gently. Direct heat scrambles them.

quiz.q: Why keep pasta water for carbonara?
options: It thins the sauce and helps it coat the pasta
quiz.explain: Pasta water loosens the egg sauce so it coats the pasta.

days.title: Cacio e Pepe: Cheese and Pepper Pasta
days.goal: Make cacio e pepe, a simple Roman pasta.

video.title: Cacio e Pepe, a Recipe for Beginners

steps: Cacio e pepe means cheese and pepper in Italian.
Cook pasta in a small amount of water so it is very starchy.
Mix grated cheese with black pepper and a little pasta water into a paste.
Toss hot pasta with the paste until creamy.
Serve at once with more cheese on top.
days.task: Make cacio e pepe.
days.challenge: Make it again and adjust the pepper to your taste.

quiz.q: What does cacio e pepe mean?
quiz.explain: Cacio e pepe is Italian for cheese and pepper.

quiz.q: Why cook pasta in little water?
options: So the water is very starchy and makes a creamy sauce
quiz.explain: Very starchy water helps the cheese form a creamy sauce.

quiz.q: How many main ingredients does cacio e pepe have?
quiz.explain: Cacio e pepe needs only pasta, cheese, and black pepper.

days.title: Homemade Pasta: From Scratch
days.goal: Make fresh pasta at home.

video.title: Chicken Fried Rice

steps: Mix flour and eggs into a dough. Knead for 10 minutes.
Cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Roll the dough out thin with a rolling pin.
Cut into strips for noodles or squares for other shapes.
Cook fresh pasta for only 2 to 3 minutes.
days.task: Make fresh pasta from scratch.
days.challenge: Cook it with a simple tomato sauce.

quiz.q: What is fresh pasta made from?
quiz.explain: Fresh pasta is flour and eggs kneaded into a dough.

quiz.q: Why rest pasta dough?
options: Resting makes it soft and easy to roll
quiz.explain: Resting relaxes the dough so it rolls out thin.

quiz.q: How long does fresh pasta cook?
quiz.explain: Fresh pasta is thin, so it cooks in 2 to 3 minutes.

days.title: Week 1 Project: A Pasta Night
days.goal: Cook three pasta dishes for your household.

video.title: Grilled Chicken Sandwich

steps: Pick three pastas: tomato spaghetti, carbonara, and cacio e pepe.
Write a shopping list and costs.
Cook each dish one at a time, starting with the slowest.
Serve all three and let everyone taste each one.
Ask which pasta they liked best and why.
days.task: Cook three pasta dishes in one night.
days.challenge: Cost the night and work out the price per person.

quiz.q: Why cook one pasta dish at a time?
options: So each dish is hot and fresh
quiz.explain: Pasta goes soft fast, so cook each dish fresh.

quiz.q: Why ask tasters which pasta they liked best?
options: It tells you what to cook again
quiz.explain: Taster feedback shows your best dishes.

quiz.q: What should a pasta night have?
quiz.explain: Three different pastas show your range.

project.title: Cook a Pasta Night
project.brief: Cook tomato spaghetti, carbonara, and cacio e pepe in one night.

days.title: Chicken Fried Rice
days.goal: Make chicken fried rice, continental style.

video.title: How to Cook Pasta

steps: Use cold, day-old rice. Fresh rice turns mushy.
Fry chicken first, then set it aside.
Fry onion, garlic, and vegetables.
Add rice and soy sauce. Toss on high heat.
Add the chicken back and serve hot.
days.task: Make chicken fried rice.
days.challenge: Make a second version with different vegetables.

quiz.q: Why use day-old rice for fried rice?
options: Cold rice stays separate instead of turning mushy
quiz.explain: Cold, dry rice fries into separate grains.

quiz.q: Why fry chicken first and set it aside?
options: So it does not overcook while the rice fries
quiz.explain: Chicken cooked first and added back at the end stays tender.

quiz.q: What does soy sauce add?
options: A deep savoury taste and colour
quiz.explain: Soy sauce adds a deep savoury taste and a golden colour.

days.title: Egg Fried Rice: Quick and Tasty
days.goal: Make egg fried rice in 10 minutes.

video.title: How to Cook Roast Chicken and Vegetables

steps: Scramble eggs first, then set them aside.
Fry onion and garlic in oil.
Add cold rice and toss on high heat.
Add soy sauce and the scrambled eggs.
Serve hot with spring onions on top.
days.task: Make egg fried rice.
days.challenge: Add chicken or prawns to make it a full meal.

quiz.q: Why scramble eggs first?
options: So they do not overcook while the rice fries
quiz.explain: Eggs cook in seconds. Adding them back at the end keeps them tender.

quiz.q: Why use cold rice?
quiz.explain: Cold rice fries into separate grains instead of mush.

quiz.q: How long does egg fried rice take?
quiz.explain: Egg fried rice is fast: about 10 minutes.

days.title: Roast Chicken and Vegetables
days.goal: Roast a whole chicken with vegetables.

video.title: Chicken Egg Fried Rice

steps: Season chicken with salt, pepper, and garlic.
Cut vegetables into similar sizes and toss in oil.
Roast at 200°C, chicken on top of the vegetables.
Cook until juices run clear and the thickest part reaches 75°C.
Rest for 10 minutes before cutting.
days.task: Roast a whole chicken with vegetables.
days.challenge: Cut it into 8 pieces and serve it.

quiz.q: Why rest roast chicken?
options: Juices spread back so the meat stays moist
quiz.explain: Cutting at once lets juices run out. Resting keeps them in.

quiz.q: What temperature must chicken reach?
quiz.explain: Chicken must reach 75°C inside to be safe.

quiz.q: Why put vegetables under the chicken?
options: Chicken juices drip down and flavour them
quiz.explain: The drippings flavour the vegetables.

days.title: Grilled Chicken Sandwich
days.goal: Make a grilled chicken sandwich.

video.title: How to Make Pasta at Home By Food Fusion | Easy Step-by-Step Tutorial

steps: Grill chicken breast until cooked through.
Toast bread or a bun on the grill.
Add lettuce, tomato, and a sauce you like.
Put the chicken in the sandwich and cut it in half.
Serve hot with chips or salad.
days.task: Make a grilled chicken sandwich.
days.challenge: Make a second one with a different sauce and compare.

quiz.q: How do you know grilled chicken is done?
options: The inside is white all the way through, not pink
quiz.explain: Chicken must be white inside, not pink, to be safe.

quiz.q: Why toast the bread?
options: Toasted bread holds the filling without going soggy
quiz.explain: Toasted bread stays firm and does not go soggy.

quiz.q: What goes well with a chicken sandwich?
quiz.explain: Chips or salad are the classic partners.

days.title: Creamy Chicken Pasta
days.goal: Make creamy chicken pasta.

video.title: Easy Homemade Pasta Recipe | From Scratch in No Time!

steps: Fry chicken pieces until cooked. Set aside.
Fry garlic and mushrooms in the same pan.
Add cream and simmer gently for 5 minutes.
Add cooked pasta and the chicken. Toss well.
Serve with grated cheese on top.
days.task: Make creamy chicken pasta.
days.challenge: Try a version with spinach added.

quiz.q: Why fry chicken first and set it aside?
options: So it does not overcook while the sauce cooks
quiz.explain: Chicken cooked first and added back at the end stays tender.

quiz.q: Why simmer cream gently?
quiz.explain: Cream on high heat can split. Gentle heat keeps it smooth.

quiz.q: What does cream add to pasta?
quiz.explain: Cream makes a rich, smooth sauce.

days.title: Continental Rice Dishes
days.goal: Cook continental rice dishes.

video.title: Easy Recipe Pasta Carbonara Italian Cooking

steps: Try a simple pilau: fry onion and spices, add rice and stock.
Try a vegetable rice: rice with mixed vegetables and herbs.
Use stock, not water, for more flavour.
Cook on low heat with the lid on. Do not lift the lid.
Rest for 10 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
days.task: Cook a pilau rice.
days.challenge: Cook a vegetable rice and compare.

quiz.q: Why cook rice in stock, not water?
options: Stock adds flavour the rice absorbs
quiz.explain: Rice cooked in stock absorbs all that flavour.

quiz.q: Why not lift the lid while rice cooks?
options: It lets steam out and ruins the cooking
quiz.explain: Rice cooks in trapped steam. Lifting the lid lets it out.

quiz.q: Why rest rice after cooking?
options: So the steam finishes cooking and the grains firm up
quiz.explain: Resting lets moisture even out so rice is fluffy.

days.title: Week 2 Project: A Continental Dinner
days.goal: Cook a continental dinner for your household.

video.title: How To Make Italian Spaghetti with Tomato Sauce / Kids Favourite

steps: Pick the menu: a pasta dish, a rice dish, and roast chicken.
Write a shopping list and costs.
Start the roast chicken first since it takes longest.
Cook the pasta and rice while the chicken roasts.
Serve all three together and ask for feedback.
days.task: Cook a continental dinner with three dishes.
days.challenge: Cost the dinner and work out the price per person.

quiz.q: Why start the roast chicken first?
options: It takes the longest, so it starts first
quiz.explain: Start with what takes longest so all food finishes together.

quiz.q: What should a continental dinner have?
options: A pasta dish, a rice dish, and a protein
quiz.explain: A mix of pasta, rice, and protein makes a full dinner.

quiz.q: Why cost the dinner?
options: So you know the price per person
quiz.explain: Costing tells you what to charge if you sell it.

project.title: Cook a Continental Dinner
project.brief: Cook a pasta dish, a rice dish, and roast chicken, served together.
checks: Roast chicken cooked through and juicy

days.title: Continental Soups: Creamy and Clear
days.goal: Make continental soups.

video.title: Cacio e Pepe, a Recipe for Beginners

steps: Cream of tomato soup: cook tomatoes, blend, add cream.
Chicken soup: boil chicken with vegetables and herbs.
Blend smooth soups with a blender. Be careful: hot soup splashes.
Season well. Taste and adjust salt.
Serve with bread.
days.task: Make a creamy tomato soup.
days.challenge: Make a chicken soup and compare.

quiz.q: How do you make a soup creamy?
options: Blend it smooth and add cream
quiz.explain: Blending smooth and adding cream makes a creamy soup.

quiz.q: Why be careful blending hot soup?
options: Hot soup splashes and can burn
quiz.explain: Hot soup in a blender can splash and burn you.

quiz.q: What goes well with soup?
quiz.explain: Bread is the classic partner for soup.

days.title: Salads: Fresh and Simple
days.goal: Make continental salads.

video.title: Chicken Fried Rice

steps: Wash and dry salad leaves. Wet leaves make dressing slide off.
Add tomato, cucumber, and onion.
Make a dressing: 3 parts oil to 1 part lemon juice or vinegar, with salt.
Toss just before serving so leaves stay crisp.
Add cheese or chicken to make it a full meal.
days.task: Make a simple salad with dressing.
days.challenge: Make a chicken salad and serve it as a meal.

quiz.q: Why dry salad leaves?
quiz.explain: Wet leaves repel dressing, so the salad tastes watery.

quiz.q: What is the classic dressing ratio?
quiz.explain: Three parts oil to one part acid gives a balanced dressing.

quiz.q: Why toss salad just before serving?
quiz.explain: Dressing left on leaves makes them go soft.

days.title: Continental Breakfast: Eggs and More
days.goal: Cook a continental breakfast.

video.title: Grilled Chicken Sandwich

steps: Fry or scramble eggs.
Grill tomatoes and mushrooms.
Toast bread and add butter.
Add cheese or cold meat if you like.
Serve with tea, coffee, or juice.
days.task: Cook a continental breakfast.
days.challenge: Time it and try to finish in 30 minutes.

quiz.q: What is in a continental breakfast?
options: Eggs, toast, grilled tomatoes, and cheese or cold meat
quiz.explain: A continental breakfast has eggs, toast, grilled tomatoes, and cheese or cold meat.

quiz.q: Why grill tomatoes for breakfast?
options: Grilling softens them and adds flavour
quiz.explain: Grilled tomatoes are soft and tasty with eggs.

quiz.q: How long should breakfast take?
quiz.explain: A simple breakfast takes about 30 minutes.

days.title: Stir Fry: Continental Style
days.goal: Make a continental stir fry.

video.title: How to Cook Pasta

steps: Cut chicken and vegetables into similar small sizes.
Get the pan very hot and add oil.
Cook in small batches so food fries, not steams.
Add sauce at the end and toss for 30 seconds.
Serve over rice or noodles.
days.task: Make a chicken and vegetable stir fry.
days.challenge: Make a vegetable-only stir fry and compare.

quiz.q: Why cut stir fry ingredients small?
quiz.explain: Small pieces cook quickly on high heat.

quiz.q: Why cook in small batches?
options: A crowded pan steams food instead of frying it
quiz.explain: Too much food drops the pan temperature and food goes soggy.

quiz.q: When does sauce go in?
options: At the end, tossed for 30 seconds
quiz.explain: Sauce added last coats and glazes without burning.

days.title: Costing Continental Dishes
days.goal: Work out what continental dishes cost.

video.title: How to Cook Roast Chicken and Vegetables

steps: List every ingredient with its price.
Add gas and packaging costs.
Divide the total by the number of portions.
Charge 2 to 3 times the food cost for a profit.
Compare with restaurants near you.
days.task: Cost a pasta dish and set its selling price.
days.challenge: Cost a roast chicken dinner the same way.

quiz.q: What is the cost per portion?
options: Total ingredient cost divided by portions
quiz.explain: Cost per portion is the ingredient cost for one serving.

quiz.q: Why charge 2 to 3 times the food cost?
options: To cover gas, packaging, and your time, and still make a profit
quiz.explain: The extra covers all the costs beyond ingredients and leaves profit.

quiz.q: Why compare with local restaurants?
options: So your price is fair for your area
quiz.explain: Local prices tell you what customers expect to pay.

days.title: Continental Cooking Mistakes and Fixes
days.goal: Fix the commonest continental cooking problems.

video.title: Chicken Egg Fried Rice

steps: Pasta went mushy? You cooked it too long or did not use enough water.
Sauce is too thin? Simmer it longer or add a little pasta water.
Chicken is dry? You overcooked it or did not rest it.
Rice is sticky? You did not rinse it or you stirred it too much.
Write down each problem and fix.
days.task: Fix one continental cooking problem you have had.
days.challenge: Cook a dish and write down what went right and wrong.

quiz.q: Why did pasta go mushy?
quiz.explain: Overcooking makes pasta soft and mushy.

quiz.q: How do you thicken a thin sauce?
quiz.explain: Simmering lets water evaporate and the sauce thicken.

quiz.q: Why is chicken dry?
options: It was overcooked or not rested
quiz.explain: Overcooking dries chicken out. Resting keeps juices in.

days.title: Week 3 Project: A Continental Feast
days.goal: Cook a full continental feast.

video.title: How to Make Pasta at Home By Food Fusion | Easy Step-by-Step Tutorial

steps: Pick the menu: pasta, rice, chicken, and a salad.
Write a shopping list and costs.
Start the chicken first since it takes longest.
Cook pasta and rice while the chicken roasts.
Serve everything together and photograph the table.
days.task: Cook a continental feast for your household.
days.challenge: Serve it to a guest and ask for their favourite dish.

quiz.q: Why start the chicken first?
quiz.explain: Slow food starts first so all food finishes together.

quiz.q: What should a continental feast have?
options: Pasta, rice, chicken, and a salad
quiz.explain: A feast balances pasta, rice, chicken, and salad.

quiz.q: Why photograph your food?
options: Photos track your progress and show customers later
quiz.explain: Photos record your work and become your portfolio if you sell food.

project.title: Cook a Continental Feast
project.brief: Cook pasta, rice, chicken, and a salad, served together.

days.title: Cooking for Events: Continental Menus
days.goal: Plan continental food for events.

video.title: Easy Homemade Pasta Recipe | From Scratch in No Time!

steps: Offer a pasta dish, a rice dish, and a chicken dish.
Add a salad and a dessert like a simple cake.
Cook in bulk: big pots of pasta and rice.
Keep food warm in a low oven or chafing dishes.
Serve with drinks and take photos.
days.task: Plan a continental menu for 20 people on paper.
days.challenge: Cook one dish from it for a group.

quiz.q: What should an event menu have?
options: Pasta, rice, chicken, salad, and dessert
quiz.explain: A full event menu balances pasta, rice, chicken, salad, and dessert.

quiz.q: Why cook in bulk for events?
quiz.explain: Bulk cooking serves a crowd efficiently.

quiz.q: How do you keep event food warm?
options: In a low oven or chafing dishes
quiz.explain: A low oven or chafing dishes hold food hot safely.

days.title: Selling Continental Food: First Steps
days.goal: Take your first steps toward selling continental food.

video.title: Easy Recipe Pasta Carbonara Italian Cooking

steps: Pick 3 or 4 dishes to sell. Keep the menu small.
Set your prices from your costing work.
Take clear photos of your dishes in good light.
Tell friends and family first. Ask them to share.
Take orders in advance so you cook only what is sold.
days.task: Take photos of your best continental dishes and show them to three people.
days.challenge: Take one real order, even a small one, and deliver it on time.

quiz.q: Why start with only 3 or 4 dishes?
options: A small menu is easier to cook well and cost
quiz.explain: A small menu keeps quality high and costing simple.

quiz.q: Why take orders in advance?
options: So you cook only what is sold and waste nothing
quiz.explain: Advance orders mean no waste and no guessing.

quiz.q: Why do photos matter?
options: Clear photos help people decide to buy
quiz.explain: People buy with their eyes first. Good photos sell food.

days.title: Your Signature Continental Dish
days.goal: Choose and perfect one continental dish you can cook brilliantly.

video.title: How To Make Italian Spaghetti with Tomato Sauce / Kids Favourite

steps: Pick the dish your household loves most from this course.
Write the recipe in your own words with exact amounts.
Cook it again, timing every step and noting problems.
Fix the problems and cook it once more.
Get someone new to taste it and give honest feedback.
days.task: Cook your signature continental dish and write the final recipe down.
days.challenge: Cook it for someone new and record what they say.

quiz.q: What is a signature dish?
options: A dish you can cook brilliantly every time
A dish with a fancy name
quiz.explain: A signature dish is one you have mastered.

quiz.q: Why write the recipe in your own words?
options: So you truly understand it and can repeat it
quiz.explain: Writing it yourself proves you understand each step.

quiz.q: Why get a new person to taste it?
quiz.explain: People who know you may be polite. New tasters are honest.

days.title: Continental Desserts: Simple Sweets
days.goal: Make simple continental desserts.

video.title: Cacio e Pepe, a Recipe for Beginners

steps: Try a fruit salad with cream.
Try a simple chocolate mousse: melted chocolate, eggs, and cream.
Try pancakes with syrup and fruit.
Serve desserts in small portions. They are rich.
Keep desserts simple. Let the main meal shine.
days.task: Make a fruit salad with cream.
days.challenge: Make pancakes with syrup and fruit.

quiz.q: What is a simple continental dessert?
options: Fruit salad with cream or pancakes
quiz.explain: Simple desserts like fruit salad and pancakes suit a continental meal.

quiz.q: Why serve desserts in small portions?
options: They are rich, so a little is enough
quiz.explain: Rich desserts are best in small portions.

quiz.q: Why keep desserts simple?
quiz.explain: A simple dessert lets the main meal be the star.

days.title: Keeping Records: Orders and Money
days.goal: Keep simple records of your continental cooking business.

video.title: Chicken Fried Rice

steps: Write down every order: what, how many, who, and when.
Write down what you spent and what you earned.
Work out your profit each week.
Note which dishes sell best and which do not.
Keep your money for cooking separate from your spending money.
days.task: Start a simple order book today, on paper or on your phone.
days.challenge: Work out your profit from one continental dinner.

quiz.q: Why write down every order?
options: So nothing is forgotten and you know what to cook
quiz.explain: Written orders stop mistakes and show what sells.

quiz.q: What is profit?
options: What is left after costs are taken from what you earned
quiz.explain: Profit is what remains after you pay for food, gas, and packaging.

quiz.q: Why keep cooking money separate?
options: So you always know if the business is making money
quiz.explain: Separate money shows the true profit of your business.

days.title: Continental Food for Special Diets
days.goal: Make continental food for special diets.

video.title: Grilled Chicken Sandwich

steps: Vegetarian pasta: use vegetables and cheese, no meat.
Gluten-free pasta: use pasta made without wheat.
Low-salt: use herbs and lemon instead of salt.
Ask customers about allergies before you cook.
Label every dish with what is in it.
days.task: Make a vegetarian pasta.
days.challenge: Make a low-salt dish and compare the taste.

quiz.q: What is vegetarian pasta?
options: Pasta with vegetables and cheese, no meat
quiz.explain: Vegetarian pasta uses vegetables and cheese, no meat.

quiz.q: What is gluten-free pasta?
quiz.explain: Gluten-free pasta is made without wheat.

quiz.q: Why label every dish?
options: So customers know what is in it
quiz.explain: Labels help customers with diets and allergies choose safely.

days.title: Continental Cooking Trends
days.goal: Try new continental ideas and see what customers like.

video.title: How to Cook Pasta

steps: Try a new pasta shape each week.
Ask customers what flavours they want.
Try a new sauce or a new herb.
Watch what other cooks serve and learn from them.
Keep what works. Drop what does not sell.
days.task: Try a new pasta shape today.
days.challenge: Ask three people what continental dish they would like to try.

quiz.q: Why try new pasta shapes?
quiz.explain: New shapes and flavours give customers a reason to return.

quiz.q: Why ask customers what they want?
options: Customers buy what they asked for
quiz.explain: Asking customers tells you what will sell.

quiz.q: Why drop dishes that do not sell?
options: So you do not waste food and time
quiz.explain: A dish that does not sell wastes food and money.

days.title: Revision: The Continental Cook's Skills Check
days.goal: Revisit the core skills of the course.

video.title: How to Cook Roast Chicken and Vegetables

steps: Cook pasta from memory, without the recipe.
Make a tomato sauce from memory.
Roast chicken from memory.
Name the main continental ingredients.
List your three strongest dishes and one to improve.
days.task: Cook a full continental meal from memory, no recipe.
days.challenge: Teach one continental dish to a friend or family member.

quiz.q: What does 'al dente' mean?
quiz.explain: Al dente means firm to the bite.

quiz.q: Why cook from memory?
options: It proves you really know the steps
quiz.explain: Cooking without a recipe shows the skills are truly learned.

quiz.q: Why teach a dish to someone else?
options: Teaching proves you really know it
quiz.explain: If you can teach it, you truly understand it.

days.title: Capstone Prep: Plan Your Final Feast
days.goal: Plan your capstone continental feast.

video.title: Chicken Egg Fried Rice

steps: Choose your capstone menu: pasta, rice, chicken, salad, and dessert.
Write the full shopping list with costs.
Write the cooking order, starting with the slowest dish.
Check you have every tool and ingredient.
Do a trial run of the hardest dish if you have time.
days.task: Write your complete capstone plan and cost it.
days.challenge: Do a trial run of your hardest capstone dish today.

quiz.q: What should your capstone show?
options: Everything you learned: pasta, rice, chicken, salad, and costing
quiz.explain: The capstone proves the whole course.

quiz.q: Why start with the slowest dish?
options: So everything finishes at the same time
quiz.explain: Slow food starts first so all food is ready together.

quiz.q: Why do a trial run?
options: To find problems before the real feast
quiz.explain: A trial run finds problems while there is still time to fix them.

capstone.title: The Continental Feast: Pasta, Rice, Chicken and More
capstone.brief: Cook a full continental feast for your household or customers: a pasta dish, a rice dish, roast chicken, a fresh salad, and a simple dessert. Cost the whole feast, serve everything hot at the same time, and collect feedback.
checks: Menu planned with a shopping list and costs per person
Pasta cooked firm, not soft, with a tasty sauce
Salad fresh and crisp with a good dressing
Feedback collected from at least one person who ate
deliverables: A photo of the finished feast on the table
Your written menu with the shopping list and costs
Your cooking order, starting with the slowest dish
Your signature continental dish recipe written in your own words
A short note on what you learned and what you will improve next
